author: massicomar
title: Frog 3
summary:
There are $N$ stones, numbered $1, 2, \ldots, N$. For each $i$ ($1 \leq i \leq N$), the height of Stone $i$ is $h_i$. Here, $h_1 < h_2 < \cdots < h_N$ holds.

There is a frog who is initially on Stone $1$. He will repeat the following action some number of times to reach Stone $N$:

- If the frog is currently on Stone $i$, jump to one of the following: Stone $i + 1, i + 2, \ldots, N$. Here, a cost of $(h_j - h_i)^2 + C$ is incurred, where $j$ is the stone to land on.

Find the minimum possible total cost incurred before the frog reaches Stone $N$.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

$N$ $C$
$h_1$ $h_2$ $\ldots$ $h_N$

Output

Print the minimum possible total cost incurred.

constraints.text: N ≤ 2e5, heights strictly increasing, cost (h_j − h_i)² + C

explanation: dp[i] = min over j < i of dp[j] + (h_i − h_j)² + C expands into lines in h_i. Slopes are monotone (heights increase), so a deque CHT gives O(N).
traps: dp values reach ~1e17; the line-intersection comparison multiplies them by slope differences, so use 128-bit or a division-based check.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i] = minimum cost to reach stone i
dp[i][j] = minimum cost to go from i to j
dp[h] = minimum cost to reach height h
options.why: Heights go up to 1e6 and aren't the stones; index by stone.

options.text: dp[i][k] = cost to reach i using k jumps
options.why: The number of jumps doesn't matter.

extraLayers.explanation: The state is easy — the hard part is the O(N²) transition.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[i] = h_i² + C + min over j of (−2h_j · h_i + dp[j] + h_j²): query a min of lines at x = h_i (convex hull trick)
dp[i] = min over all j < i of dp[j] + (h_i − h_j)² + C, by direct loop

options.why: Jumps can skip stones; sometimes one long jump beats many short ones (C is large).
That's Frog 1; here any j < i is allowed.

extraLayers.explanation: Each j contributes a line with slope −2h_j; slopes decrease and query points increase, so a monotone deque answers each query in amortized O(1).

es.explanation: dp[i] = mín sobre j < i de dp[j] + (h_i − h_j)² + C se desarrolla en rectas en h_i. Las pendientes son monótonas (las alturas crecen), así que un CHT con deque da O(N).
traps: Los valores de dp llegan a ~1e17; la comparación de intersecciones de rectas los multiplica por diferencias de pendientes, así que usa 128 bits o un chequeo con divisiones.

dp-state.explanation: El estado es fácil: lo difícil es la transición O(N²).

why.c: Las alturas llegan a 1e6 y no son las piedras; indexa por piedra.
why.d: La cantidad de saltos no importa.

dp-transition.explanation: Cada j aporta una recta de pendiente −2h_j; las pendientes decrecen y los puntos de consulta crecen, así que un deque monótono responde cada consulta en O(1) amortizado.

why.b: La recurrencia es correcta, pero son 2e10 operaciones.
why.c: Los saltos pueden saltarse piedras; a veces un salto largo le gana a muchos cortos (C es grande).
why.d: Ese es Frog 1; acá se permite cualquier j < i.
